headline: Iran standoff, a rate hike and the midterm countdown dominate the week
summary: Stalled U.S.-Iran diplomacy kept oil above US$110 and helped push the Bank of Canada into a rate hike, while the Canada-U.S. trade file stayed stuck ahead of Tuesday's midterms. In Ontario, the fall economic statement showed a bigger deficit, and a Bridle Path home invasion drew national attention.

top.headline: Iran weighs U.S. letter as Qatar steps up Hormuz mediation
top.what: Iran kept the Strait of Hormuz shut and set conditions while Qatar mediated; by week's end Tehran floated a two-day reopening plan if the U.S. cooperates.
top.why: Oil prices drive fuel and grocery costs in Ontario.

top.headline: Carney widens trade push as U.S. deal stays out of reach
top.what: Cabinet ministers told CTV News this is a 'now or maybe never' moment for auto tariffs but doubt Trump will compromise, after Ambassador Pete Hoekstra reportedly said Canada could be blamed for midterm losses.
top.why: U.S. tariffs threaten Ontario auto and steel jobs.

top.headline: Economy stalls in August, two days after Bank of Canada's hike
top.what: The Bank of Canada raised its key rate to 2.50% on Oct. 28, then data showed the economy stalled in August.
top.why: Higher rates raise borrowing costs for GTA households.

top.headline: Chow re-elected; GTA voters oust mayors in Mississauga, Hamilton, Oakville and Milton
top.what: Olivia Chow won a second term as Toronto mayor, and final counts show voters across the region replaced several long-serving incumbents.
top.why: New councils will shape local taxes, housing and transit.

top.headline: Early voting runs about 10 million ahead of 2022 as midterms near
top.what: More than 43 million early ballots, about 10 million ahead of 2022, as Democrats lead national polls and Senate control hinges on a few toss-ups.
top.why: Control of Congress affects tariffs on Canada.

top.headline: Ontario deficit grows to $16.9 billion; balance pushed to 2029-30
top.what: Ontario's fall economic statement projects a $16.9-billion deficit this year and pushes a balanced budget to 2029-30, with an $8-billion business write-off.
top.why: Sets provincial spending and the deficit path.

top.headline: Joly won't meet Stelco owner's CEO without a plan to restore jobs
top.what: Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says she will only meet Cleveland-Cliffs CEO Lourenco Goncalves once the company produces a plan and timeline to bring back laid-off Stelco workers.
top.why: Hamilton steel jobs hang on the outcome.

top.headline: Russian strike cuts power in parts of Kyiv as Canada pledges €500 million
top.what: A Russian strike cut power to parts of Kyiv as Canada pledged €500 million toward an international loan for Ukraine's 2027 budget gap.
top.why: Canada is a major backer of Ukraine's defence.
